_doc: Site-wide settings. 'basePath' must start with a slash when deploying under a repository subpath (e.g. '/metal2humanoid'); leave it empty for a root deployment. 'contact' is the single place to change who receives course and sponsorship email (name, email, title shown next to the address). 'draft.enabled' adds a visible notice, a noindex/nofollow meta tag, and a robots.txt that disallows crawling; set it to false when the content is final. 'apply' is the application call to action: when enabled (and its deadline has not passed at build time) a banner is shown under the header on every page, an 'Apply' pill in the navigation, and the hero's first button; set enabled to false or let the deadline pass to remove it.
name: Metal2Humanoid
tagline: Building a Humanoid Robot from the Ground Up
description: Metal2Humanoid is a proposed non-credit MIT IAP 2027 course: four weeks of integrated lecture-lab sessions in which every student builds an actuator, teams assemble and program a custom humanoid, and the course ends with a public showcase on January 29, 2027.

status.approvalNote: Proposed as a non-credit MIT IAP 2027 activity; approval, meeting times, and rooms are provisional.

registration.label: Apply to attend
registration.note: Applications from current MIT students are open until Friday, December 12, 2026.

hbrn.name: Homebrew Robotics Network
hbrn.relationship: Metal2Humanoid is organized by its instructors together with members of the Homebrew Robotics Network (HBRN), the builder community behind the initiative.
hbrn.blurb: The Homebrew Robotics Network is a community of builders working toward open, accessible, reproducible robotics: hardware that can be built from widely available parts, documented well enough for others to repeat, and shared under open licenses. For Metal2Humanoid, HBRN hardware contributors lead the robot design and the Week 1 actuator materials, and the instructors lead the simulation, locomotion, and task weeks.
hbrn.next: The Metal2Humanoid built in the course, a larger custom humanoid around commercial actuators, is released openly afterwards, together with the lab guides and notebooks, so that other groups can repeat the course. Further out, HBRN is exploring two companion efforts that may extend the materials: OSH Atlas, an atlas of open humanoid projects and resources, and UMOJA, a framework for assessing and comparing open humanoid designs, both possible future extensions for documentation, resource sharing, and benchmarking.

apply.text: About 20 places in six teams, January 4–29, 2027, non-credit. No prior hardware, control, or machine learning experience is required. The application is a short Google Form.
